subject: English
topic: Cloze Test — Environment and Reading Passages

questions.stem:
Read and answer Q1-Q5:
'The environment is facing (1)______ threats due to (2)______ human activities. Deforestation, (3)______ of fossil fuels, and improper waste disposal are the major (4)______ of environmental degradation. It is now (5)______ that we take immediate action to protect our planet.'

Q1 — blank (1):

options.option_text: minor (contradicts the serious tone and call for immediate action)
immense (correct: immense threats = very large, serious; fits the critical tone ✓)
imaginary (contradicts the factual context)
temporary (contradicts the urgency of 'immediate action')

questions.explanation: B is correct. The passage describes serious environmental problems and demands immediate action — the threats must be IMMENSE (very large/severe). 'Minor', 'imaginary', and 'temporary' would undermine the urgency.

options.option_text: virtuous (morally excellent; contradicts causing environmental damage)
beneficial (advantageous; contradicts causing environmental threats)
irresponsible (correct: irresponsible = lacking care; human activities lacking environmental responsibility cause damage ✓)
constructive (helpful/building; contradicts environmental degradation)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Human activities that threaten the environment are IRRESPONSIBLE (lacking care or responsibility). All positive words (virtuous, beneficial, constructive) contradict causing environmental harm.

options.option_text: conservation (preservation; the opposite of a harmful activity)
combustion (correct: combustion/burning of fossil fuels releases pollutants — a major environmental problem ✓)
recycling (environmentally positive; not a cause of degradation)
protection (protecting fossil fuels is not an environmental threat)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The passage lists harmful activities: deforestation + COMBUSTION of fossil fuels + improper waste disposal. All three are causes of environmental degradation. 'Conservation', 'recycling', and 'protection' are environmentally positive — wrong context.

questions.stem: Q4 — blank (4): '...are the major (4)______ of environmental degradation.'

options.option_text: solutions (solutions fix degradation, not cause it)
causes (correct: deforestation, fossil fuels, waste disposal are CAUSES of degradation ✓)
benefits (positive outcomes; contradicts degradation)
remedies (remedies cure problems; contradicts listing problems)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The three items listed are CAUSES of environmental degradation. 'Solutions', 'benefits', and 'remedies' all imply positive interventions — contradicting the negative framing.

questions.stem: Q5 — blank (5): 'It is now (5)______ that we take immediate action...'

options.option_text: optional (not required; contradicts 'immediate action' needed)
unnecessary (not needed; contradicts urgent tone)
imperative (correct: imperative = absolutely necessary; standard call-to-action word ✓)
unlikely (not probable; contradicts the call for action)

questions.explanation: C is correct. IMPERATIVE = of vital importance; absolutely necessary. 'It is now imperative that we act' is a standard formal English construction for urgent calls to action. All other options weaken or contradict the urgency.

questions.stem:
Read and answer Q6-Q10:
'Reading is one of the most (6)______ habits one can (7)______. Books (8)______ our imagination, increase our (9)______, and help us understand the world better. People who read (10)______ are generally more empathetic and articulate.'

Q6 — blank (6):

options.option_text: harmful (contradicts praising reading)
trivial (unimportant; contradicts the positive passage)
beneficial (correct: 'most beneficial habits' = very good habit; matches the praising tone ✓)
tedious (boring; contradicts the positive description)

questions.explanation: C is correct. The passage praises reading — 'one of the most BENEFICIAL habits.' The rest confirms this with positive effects (imagination, vocabulary, empathy). All other options carry negative meanings.

questions.stem: Q7 — blank (7): '...one of the most beneficial habits one can (7)______.'

options.option_text: avoid (stay away from; contradicts cultivating a habit)
cultivate (correct: 'cultivate a habit' = develop and nurture a habit over time ✓)
neglect (fail to attend to; negative connotation)
destroy (completely ruin; contradicts building a habit)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'CULTIVATE a habit' is the standard English idiom = to develop and nurture a habit. Think of cultivating crops — you tend them carefully over time. Avoid, neglect, and destroy all have negative meanings.

options.option_text: restrict (limit; contradicts the positive benefit)
stifle (prevent or constrain; negative)
stimulate (correct: 'stimulate imagination' = activate and encourage creativity ✓)
reduce (make smaller; contradicts expanding imagination)

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'STIMULATE imagination' = activate, inspire, encourage creative thinking. Standard phrase for the positive effect of reading on creativity. All wrong options restrict or reduce imagination.

questions.stem: Q9 — blank (9): 'Books stimulate our imagination, increase our (9)______...'

options.option_text: ignorance (lack of knowledge; contradicts learning from reading)
vocabulary (correct: reading increases vocabulary — well-known benefit ✓)
confusion (contradicts positive benefits)
laziness (contradicts productive benefits of reading)

questions.explanation: B is correct. A widely accepted benefit of reading is building VOCABULARY (range and knowledge of words). All other options are negative attributes that contradict reading's benefits.

questions.stem: Q10 — blank (10): 'People who read (10)______ are generally more empathetic and articulate.'

options.option_text: rarely (infrequent reading wouldn't produce strong benefits)
reluctantly (unwillingly; wouldn't produce positive habits)
occasionally (from time to time; too infrequent for these strong effects)
regularly (correct: consistent, frequent reading produces empathy and vocabulary ✓)

questions.explanation: D is correct. People who read REGULARLY (consistently and often) develop empathy and articulateness. 'Rarely' and 'occasionally' imply infrequent reading — insufficient for these strong effects. 'Reluctantly' implies unwillingness — not a habit that would yield these results.
